summary: Bind Cloud KMS encrypt/decrypt hot paths to typed tenant/cell/region placement boundaries. API boundary contexts now require X-Region-Code and X-Cell-Id, validate them as canonical region/cell values before authorization/idempotency, compare them against the registered KMS key placement before ledger or receipt mutation, thread them into domain KMS use requests, and keep idempotency fingerprints placement-aware.

baseline_diff.before: Cloud KMS key creation carried typed RegionCode and CellId, but encrypt/decrypt API and domain use requests carried only tenant/key/body data. Hot-path crypto authorization could not prove the caller's region/cell matched the key's cell-local HSM placement.
baseline_diff.after: Cloud KMS API boundary contexts carry region and cell_id, validate missing/invalid/mismatched placement before authorization/idempotency/domain mutation, domain KmsEncryptRequest/KmsDecryptRequest enforce request region/cell against the KmsKey, and OpenAPI requires X-Region-Code plus X-Cell-Id for encrypt/decrypt.

repo_authority_used.establishes: Tier 3 cells host cloud-secrets data-plane KMS keys and per-cell HSM partitions; per-tenant KMS root keys live in the cell HSM; hot-path tenant serving resolves in the home cell and cross-cell hot-path serving is forbidden.
Data-residency hard-stops use cell-pin/cell-id decisions and forbid work when cell_id does not match the required cell; cell-id is the named residency audit surface.
CS-CLOUD-KMS-002 acceptance criteria require typed tenant/cell/region boundary metadata and no KMS operation without matching tenant/cell/region context.

implementation_notes: Reused existing oya-cloud-region-domain RegionCode and CellId types instead of adding another placement abstraction.

Kept tenant checks in existing boundary/principal/body validation and added region/cell checks to the same CloudKmsApiBoundaryContext to avoid splitting tooling/tools or creating a second boundary object prematurely.

Preserved domain purity: the domain receives region/cell strings and validates them into RegionCode/CellId against the already-typed KmsKey; API remains responsible for transport header names and response error shaping.

Placement mismatch for a known key returns Kms(ResourceRegionMismatch) or Kms(CellPlacementMismatch) before idempotency ledger mutation; unknown-key behavior remains not-found through existing KMS domain path.

findings: The slice adds two existing primitive fields to the existing boundary and domain request structs rather than creating a new abstraction stack.
KMS key use is bound to cell-local HSM placement, matching the repo's cellular architecture doctrine for hot-path intra-cell execution.
Tests clear authorization surfaces on missing-header cases to prove boundary validation runs before auth and assert empty idempotency ledger plus zero receipts on placement failures.
Header names are explicit in OpenAPI and error details point to header.X-Region-Code/header.X-Cell-Id.
RED/GREEN TDD, package regression, clippy, fmt, and Oya gates cover the claimed behavior.

alternatives_named: Only validate placement inside the domain after idempotency lookup
Parse placement from key_id strings only
Add typed boundary fields at API plus domain enforcement
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The selected path proves placement before auth/idempotency side effects while keeping domain enforcement as a second line of defense.
rejected_reasons: Domain-only validation would still allow placement failures to enter the API idempotency ledger.
Key-id parsing alone does not prove caller cell matches the registered KMS key cell.

findings: Known-key region/cell drift fails before ledger or receipt mutation; no key/plaintext/ciphertext material is added to boundary metadata.
Boundary parsing is constant-size and key lookup uses the existing in-memory directory iterator; no network or provider I/O is introduced.
Cell/region headers make the KMS hot path auditable against the cell residency boundary required by ADR-0248 and ADR-0304.
The change is isolated to KMS API/domain request shapes and OpenAPI headers; rollback is a single ChangeSet revert.
API errors now identify placement boundary header fields; dedicated placement metrics/traces remain deferred to gateway/observability work.
OpenAPI exposes exact required placement headers for SDK/gateway implementers.
Clean architecture remains intact: API owns transport headers/errors/idempotency; domain owns key placement invariants; adapters remain provider-command translation only.

remaining_risks: API gateway/proto carriers are still future work outside this API crate slice.
Provider adapters still receive provider request shapes without explicit region/cell fields; they remain deterministic command translators and do not execute provider I/O in this slice.
Cloud KMS manifest still overclaims some capability/SLO/DR surfaces and is deferred to CS-CLOUD-KMS-004.
